infectious.q: How do I choose which infectious disease tests to stock?
infectious.a: Start with the high-burden combos — dengue NS1+IgM/IgG, malaria Pf/Pan, HBsAg/HCV/HIV/syphilis combos — then add single markers for regional demand. Combo devices reduce SKU count and widen diagnostic coverage.

infectious.q: Are your infectious disease tests CE-marked?
infectious.a: Selected lines carry CE marking (self-declaration under IVDD 98/79/EC via our EU Authorized Representative). Confirm the specific product's scope before ordering for a regulated market.

infectious.q: Do the tests need cold chain?
infectious.a: No — colloidal-gold lateral-flow tests are room-temperature stable, ideal for tropical and remote distribution.

doa.q: Can you build a custom drug-testing panel?
doa.a: Yes — as an OEM/ODM manufacturer we configure custom analyte panels, cut-offs, branding and cup formats (up to 14 analytes).

doa.q: What cut-off levels do you use?
doa.a: Cut-offs align with SAMHSA-style standards (e.g., THC 50 ng/mL, cocaine 150–300 ng/mL, amphetamine/methamphetamine 500–1000 ng/mL) and are configurable per market.

doa.q: Are DOA tests FDA or CE marked?
doa.a: Selected DOA lines carry CE marking; some analytes (AMP, BZO, COC, THC, MET, MOP) are listed as FDA lines on the company site — request the specific 510(k)/CE documentation.

cardiac-tumor.q: Are cardiac markers quantitative or qualitative?
cardiac-tumor.a: Most are qualitative or semi-quantitative lateral-flow devices for triage; some markers are also available in fluorescence quantitative formats on request.

cardiac-tumor.q: Which cardiac panel should I start with?
cardiac-tumor.a: Troponin I + CK-MB + Myoglobin is the standard POC cardiac panel; add D-dimer for thrombosis assessment.

womens-health.q: What retail packaging options do you offer?
womens-health.a: Private-label retail packaging, including midstream, cassette and strip formats, with custom branding.

womens-health.q: Are hCG and LH tests CE/FDA marked?
womens-health.a: hCG and LH lines carry CE marking and are listed as FDA lines on the company site — request specific documentation.

other.q: Can I mix formats in one order?
other.a: Yes — cassette, strip and device formats can be combined to meet MOQ efficiently.

other.q: What is the MOQ for specialty assays?
other.a: Low MOQ is available for the specialty 'Other' series — request current MOQ and lead time.
